drawings.description: sous « $C_{\infty,3}$ », une longue flèche descendante aboutissant à une sphère : contour rond, équateur en ellipse (l'arc arrière interrompu), et trois gros points sur l'équateur, deux sur l'arc avant et un sur l'arc arrière.
drawings.kind: sphere with three marked points on its equator, reached by an arrow
drawings.notes: As on the page: the label C_{infinity,3}, the long arrow down to the top of the sphere, the round outline, the equator as an ellipse whose back arc is dashed (he broke it into three strokes), and three heavy points on the equator, two on the front arc and one on the back arc, each placed on the computed ellipse. A fourth, much smaller dot on the front arc between the two heavy points is drawn small (a pen rest or a fourth mark: see review). Nothing struck. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop: outline, equator, arrow, label and the three points fall on the page; unchanged. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à gauche de « $\omega_1, \omega_2$, $\omega_2/\omega_1 = \tau$ », une sphère couverte de hachures obliques : contour rond, équateur en ellipse, trois gros points, un en haut et un en bas sur le contour, un sur l'arc avant de l'équateur.
drawings.kind: sphere covered with oblique hatching, three marked points
drawings.notes: As on the page, overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop and redrawn 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5): the outline is three strokes, not a round circle (an upper arc from the left through the top point to the right, a left lower arc and a right lower arc ending at the bottom point); the equator is a heavy back arc and a front arc that begins as the upper left part of the outline and runs through the front point to the right side; the hatching is one zigzag stroke of six legs, drawn as he drew it (from beyond the top point down to the left, up to the upper right, down to the lower left, up to the right, down to the lower left, back to the right along a curve, and a short leg down). Three heavy points: top and bottom on the outline, one on the front arc of the equator. The earlier redraw (round outline, ellipse equator lying 3 units too low at the back, five parallel hatching strokes not his) is replaced. Disagreement with the note of the transcription, which says « deux points marqués »: three are on the page. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
drawings.disagreement: The note says « deux points marqués »; the page has three heavy points (top and bottom of the outline, and one on the front of the equator).

drawings.description: l'ellipse décrite dans le texte : deux croix à gauche, marquées $0$ et \uncertain{$2^{3}\cdot 3^{4}$}, un gros point à droite, deux marques épaisses en pointe de flèche sur le bord (en bas et en haut à droite) ; au-dessus un court trait horizontal, à gauche un trait vertical interrompu, à droite « $C_{1,1}$ ».
drawings.kind: ellipse with two crosses, a point and arrow marks on its rim
drawings.notes: The ellipse; inside, two small crosses at the left with their labels below them, 0 and the product 2^3.3^4 (set as the transcription reads it, where it is marked uncertain; on the page the last digit could also be a 9), and a heavy point at the right; on the rim two heavy marks: at the bottom an arrow pointing right, and at the upper right a heavy stretch of the rim with a small blackened wedge hanging under its left end (the transcription's second « pointe de flèche »; which way it points cannot be read, so it is drawn as it stands); above the ellipse a short horizontal stroke with a heavy end on each side; at the left a broken vertical stroke; at the right the label C_{1,1}. The transcription describes this figure in an editorial sentence of the text (« Une ellipse marquée de deux croix ... »). Redrawn and overlaid 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session). The ellipse refitted to the outline (0.6 unit lower, 0.4 unit wider; his outline bulges about a unit beyond it at the upper right), the upper rim mark drawn as the heavy stretch and wedge it is (it was a plain heavy stroke inside the rim); the crosses, the point, the lower arrow, the strokes and the labels lie on their ink. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: à droite de « $D_n^{*} = \ldots$ », un pentagone découpé en secteurs depuis son centre : cinq sommets marqués (celui du haut d'un petit cercle, les autres de gros points), un gros point au centre, et une douzaine de rayons issus du centre, vers les sommets et vers les côtés, celui qui va au sommet de droite épaissi.
drawings.kind: pentagon cut into sectors from its centre
drawings.notes: The pentagon between its five vertices (top vertex ringed, the four others heavy points), the heavy centre, and thirteen rays from the centre, all drawn from the one centre point: to the top vertex; to the upper right side (two, both ending on it); to the right vertex (heavy); one to the right stopping short of the right side; two to the lower right, ending on the right side and on the bottom side; one straight down, crossing the bottom side; one to the lower left stopping short of the side; two reaching the lower left side; one to the left stopping just short of the left vertex; one to the upper left stopping inside. Rays that reach a side end on it (computed). Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the second ray to the upper right side (from the centre to the side, between the ray to the side and the heavy ray) was missing, and the ray to the right ends short of the side on the page, not on it. Several rays start a little away from the centre on the page and are slightly curved (drawn straight). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: au-dessous, une ligne horizontale portant sept points marqués, prolongée à gauche par deux points et à droite par trois points de suspension (le cas $n = \infty$).
drawings.kind: pointed line continued by dots on both sides (n infinite)
drawings.notes: As on the page: a horizontal line with seven marked points (its two ends and five between, unevenly spaced, each computed on the line), two dots before it at the left and three after it at the right. A stray dot under the line, near the middle, is left out. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop: the line, its seven points and the dots fall on the page; unchanged. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: au milieu de la page, deux arcs en chevron : celui de gauche terminé à gauche par une pointe de flèche, celui de droite portant une pointe de flèche vers la droite, chacun traversé d'une courte flèche transverse pointant vers le haut ; à droite, dans leur prolongement, un trait épais descendant portant un point ; au-dessous, quatre traits fins en éventail.
drawings.kind: two arcs with transverse arrows, a heavy stroke and a fan of thin strokes
drawings.notes: Two nearly straight arcs meeting (without touching) at the top: the left one ends at the left in an arrowhead, the right one carries an arrowhead pointing right near its right end; each is crossed by a short transverse arrow pointing upwards. At the right, continuing the right arc downwards, a stroke gone over in a narrow doubled heavy stretch (two strokes side by side, the second with a small hook at its upper end) carrying a heavy point, then thin, with a small barb just above its lower hook. Below, four thin strokes fanning downwards: three straight ones falling to the left and a longer curved one at the far right. Redrawn and overlaid 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session): every stroke lies on its ink within about 1 unit. The heavy stretch, drawn before as one heavy line, is two strokes on the page and is now drawn so, with the small hook at the upper end of the second and the barb above the lower hook (the two barbs left out before); whether either is meant as an arrowhead the page does not say, and they are drawn as they stand. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: à droite, un cercle divisé : sept points marqués sur le bord, un diamètre montant vers la droite et prolongé au-delà du cercle, un rayon horizontal épaissi allant du centre au bord droit, une verticale tangente à droite ; un point isolé au-dessus ; à droite la mention « $\pm\frac{1}{n}$ » ; un petit zigzag sur le diamètre, en bas à gauche.
drawings.kind: divided circle with a heavy radius, marked +-1/n
drawings.notes: The circle (an ellipse on the page, 21 by 19.8 units) with seven heavy points on it, three small dots and two small ticks; the diameter from the lower left point through the centre to the upper right point, produced beyond the circle at the upper right; the heavy radius from the centre to the point where the vertical line touches the circle at the right; the vertical line itself, from well above the circle to far below it (it runs down to 25 units under the circle); an isolated point above the circle; the label +-1/n at the right. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the circle was 1.5 units too low at the bottom and the bottom point off it; the vertical line stopped at -73 where the page has it run to -99 (bbox extended down to 0.6); the small dots on the right and lower right arcs and the two ticks on the left arc were not drawn; the label moved down onto its place. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session): the circle, its points and ticks, the diameter, the heavy radius, the vertical line, the isolated point and the label lie on their ink within about 1 unit. The small zigzag over the lower left part of the diameter, left out before, is the transcription's « petit zigzag sur le diamètre » and is drawn in darker ink than the figure on the page: now drawn through its peaks read on the scan. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: au-dessous, un cercle dont six arcs sont épaissis, alternant avec des arcs fins, et à l'intérieur une flèche courbe de rotation, montant vers la droite.
drawings.kind: circle (freehand) with alternating heavy arcs and a rotation arrow
drawings.notes: The circle, a freehand closed curve on the page (flatter at the upper right, its right side bending in towards the bottom), drawn through points read on its ink; six heavy arcs on it (a long one over the top right, one at the upper left ending in a small blackened wedge, a long one on the left, one at the right, a short one below it at the lower right, one at the bottom right), separated by thin arcs; short ticks across the circle at the ends of five heavy arcs (upper left, both ends of the left one, the lower end of the right one, the upper end of the bottom right one) and at the left end of the bottom right one; inside the circle a curved arrow turning counter-clockwise, its head pointing up. Redrawn and overlaid 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session). The circle had been drawn as a true ellipse, which ran up to 2 units inside the ink at the upper right and 3 to 4 units outside it at the lower right, where the heavy arc on the right stood off the ink: the outline and the six heavy arcs are redrawn on the ink, the ticks and the wedge (left out before) added, the arrow moved by up to 1.2 units. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: en bas de la page, une carte en forme de pentagone : cinq sommets cerclés reliés en cycle, une arête pendante issue de chacun (celle du haut finissant en fourche), un point cerclé au centre ; à droite, un astérisque.
drawings.kind: pentagonal map with ringed vertices and pendant edges; an asterisk
drawings.notes: The pentagon between its five ringed vertices (points with an open ring round each; the left one larger), the five sides, one pendant edge from each vertex (to the left with an end point; down to the left with an end point; down to the right; up to the right with an end point; and at the top a short edge to a small vertex that forks into two prongs and sends another edge to the left, to an end point above the left vertex), and a ringed point in the middle of the face. Below that end point, after a small gap, a short stroke goes down to the ring of the left vertex. At the right, apart, an asterisk of three strokes through one point. Left out: the frame of the boxed formula and its text, which run into the crop at the top right. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the right vertex was drawn 7.5 units too high (at the level of the end of its pendant edge), which bent the top and right sides; the lower right vertex, the end of the right pendant edge and the rings are moved onto the page; the short stroke under the upper left end point is drawn solid with its gap, as on the page, not dashed. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à droite de « $2 = 2\cdot 1$ », un bouquet de trois cercles : trois boucles issues d'un même gros point, vers le haut à droite, vers la droite et vers le bas.
drawings.notes: As on the page: three loops from one heavy point, each drawn as a closed curve leaving and returning to that point: one to the upper right, one to the right, one downwards. Nothing struck. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop: the three loops fall on the page within a unit; unchanged. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en haut à droite, un triangle hachuré de traits verticaux, de sommets $0$ (en bas à gauche), $\infty$ (en haut) et $1$ (à droite).
drawings.notes: As on the page: the triangle with heavy sides, its vertices labelled 0 (lower left), infinity (top) and 1 (right), and seven vertical hatching strokes standing on the base (computed on it) and stopping short of the upper sides, as he drew them: three thin ones at the left, three heavy ones in the middle, a short one at the right. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the strokes were drawn from side to base; on the page none reaches the upper sides, the left ones are thin and short. A small hook on the right side near the top is left out. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à droite de la suite exacte, une carte de quadrilatères accolés, à l'encre sur un premier tracé au crayon, aux sommets numérotés $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$ ; deux faces du haut sont couvertes de traits croisés au crayon.
drawings.kind: map of quadrilaterals with vertices numbered 0, 1, 2, 3
drawings.notes: The ink edges only, each drawn between the vertices as read, with the digits beside the vertices where he wrote them. Upper row: the quadrilateral 1-2-1-0 (top side and right side heavy, the side 0-1 heavy, one diagonal in ink) and, to its right, the quadrilateral 2-3-0-1; pencil crossed strokes in these two faces (drawn as two pencil crosses). Left: the open polygon rising from the vertex 3 at the lower left to the stroke marked 3 at the top. Lower part: the edges from the central vertex 1 to the vertices 2, 0 and 3 below it, the edges 0-1 and 2-1 to the bottom vertex 1, the heavy edge 3-2 at the left, and the detached strokes at the far left and far right. Left out: the first pencil tracing under the ink (long curved strokes across the whole figure, and an arrow to the lower right). Still differs: this is a reading of a crowded figure; several joins are uncertain (whether the thin stroke from the vertex 0 goes down to the vertex 2 below it; the strokes round the lower left vertices 3, 2, 0), some digits are hard to tell (the 1 at the top vertex, the 1 at the bottom), and which faces he meant as hatched is not settled: the note of the transcription says « certaines faces hachurées ». Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the edge from the central vertex 1 to the right vertex 0 and the edge from the lower vertex 2 to the right end an arrowhead each (they were plain lines); the left open polygon follows the page (its corner is at 13.5, -35, not 14, -32); the thin vertical stroke from the vertex 0 down is pencil, not ink; the vertical stroke left of the vertex 0 and the stroke above the top vertex moved onto the page; the pencil hatching of the two upper faces is redrawn as the strokes seen (in the right face the pencil diagonal from 2 to 0 and three strokes across it; in the left face three strokes), not as two crosses; the pencil strokes are approximate. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session): the vertices, the ink edges and the digits lie on their ink within about 1 to 2 units. Four edges inked heavy on the page and drawn thin are now heavy (the right side from the top 3 down to the right vertex, the edge from the vertex 0 down to the lower left, the edge from the central 1 down to the lower 2, the detached stroke at the far right), and the stroke from the lower vertex 2 to the vertex 0 beside it, on the page but not drawn, is added. Still differs: at the lower left several long strokes leave the vertex 3 and the vertex 0 towards the central vertex 1 and cross one another, and which of them join which vertices stays a reading (one of them starts from a short heavy stroke below the 0 and is not drawn separately); the heavy stroke down from beside the vertex 0 to the bottom vertex 1 starts about 2 units right of the 0, as on the page.

drawings.description: à gauche, une sphère : contour rond, équateur en ellipse ; sur le contour, $i$ en haut, $-i$ en bas, un gros point à gauche et un point à droite, chacun avec un chiffre peu lisible (lus $3$ et $1$) ; un point marqué d'un chiffre (lu $2$) sur l'arc arrière de l'équateur ; près du centre, $0$ entouré d'une petite boucle ; un lacet descend de $i$ vers cette boucle, et une courbe va de $i$ à $-i$ en coupant l'arc avant de l'équateur en un point marqué.
drawings.kind: sphere with its equator; marked points i, -i, 0, 1, 2, 3 and loops
drawings.notes: Redrawn 2026-11-13 as a sphere with its equator, as the editor asked (#148: « ça devrait être dessiné comme une sphère avec l'équateur »): the round outline, and the equator as one true ellipse between the left and right points on the outline (his two freehand arcs), its front half solid and its back half dashed; the marked point of the back arc and the point of the front arc where the curve from i to -i crosses are put on the ellipse (the back point lies about two units higher on the page, where his back arc bulges more). Kept from the page: i (top) and -i (bottom) on the outline, the heavy point at the left and the point at the right, 0 near the centre inside a small loop, the stroke from i down to that loop, the curve from i to -i through the front point. Digits as before, read 2 (back arc), 1 (right), 3 (left): the editor's answer (#148) asks for the sphere and does not settle them, and the transcription's note reads 1 on the back arc with nothing legible at the left and right; still to confirm. Left out: the faint pencil ovals round 0 and a short tick on the curve. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop: outline, points and curves within a unit or two. Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session): the outline, i, -i, the left and right points, the loop round 0 and the curves lie on their ink within about 1 to 2 units; the equator is the true ellipse the editor asked for (#148), so it departs from his freehand arcs by up to about 2 units, as said; nothing changed. Still differs: the three digits, as said above. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: à droite, quatre figures de lacets dans le plan. En haut : deux points $i$ et $-i$ l'un au-dessus de l'autre, reliés par deux arcs en croissant, et chacun relié par un trait double à un gros point cerclé à droite ; une longue ligne fine horizontale traverse la figure. Au milieu à gauche : $i$ en haut, $-i$ en bas, $0$ entouré d'une boucle sur un axe horizontal gradué en $1$, un trait descendant de $i$ à la boucle, un trait double de la boucle à $-i$, et deux grands arcs de $i$ à $-i$ passant à droite de $0$. Au milieu à droite : un lacet en « V » à trait double finissant par un petit cercle, avec les lettres $0$ et $1$. En bas à droite : un lacet en équerre à trait double, entourant un point et finissant par un petit cercle.
drawings.kind: four figures of loops in the plane round 0 and 1, based at i and -i
drawings.notes: Four figures. (1) Top: the points i (top) and its mate below (-i, label not legible), two crescent arcs between them, a double stroke from each to the heavy ringed point at the right (a letter is scribbled inside it: not read), an arrowhead on the upper double stroke near i; the long thin horizontal line across the figure with a dot on it. (2) Middle left: i, -i, the loop round 0 on the horizontal axis, the tick and the label 1 on the axis, the stroke from i down to the loop, the double stroke from the loop down to -i, and the two large arcs from i to -i on the right of 0 (the inner one ends just above -i; the outer one carries a small arrowhead pointing down, near its lower end). (3) Middle right: a V of double strokes, from the top down to its tip and up to a small circle at the right, with the letters 0 (at the left) and 1 (inside the V). (4) Bottom right: an L of double strokes, coming down, turning round a point inside a small loop, and running right to a small circle. Left out: the faint pencil ovals round 0 in (2), two small dots near -i, the scribble inside the ringed point of (1). Redrawn and overlaid 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 249 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session). In (2) the two large arcs were up to 2 units off their ink (outside it in their upper half, inside it in their lower half): both are redrawn through points read on the scan, the small arrowhead on the outer arc (left out before) is added, and the loop round 0 refitted (0.7 unit lower); (1), (3) and (4) lie on their ink within about 1 unit. Still differs: the label -i of the lower point of (1) is not legible (a small hooked stroke under the point may be its i): not placed; the letter scribbled inside the ringed point of (1) is not read; in (3) the letters are small and their reading 0, 1 (the transcription's) is not sure; the double strokes are drawn as two lines read on the crop and their closures at the ends are approximate (within about 1 unit).
